subject: pip:fsspec@2025.3.0
reason: The wake-word GPU synthesis toolbox only (scripts/wake-word/requirements-gpu.lock.txt): VoxCPM 2.0.3 requires datasets >=3,<4; the compatible lock selects datasets 3.6.0, which caps fsspec at 2025.3.0. It runs on the developer's machine, reads local audio and Hugging Face files, and never opens a ReferenceFileSystem; never in production. Lifted when voxcpm accepts a datasets that allows fsspec >= 2026.6.0.

subject: pip:cbor2@6.1.4
reason: Native recursion in cbor2.dumps() on a deeply nested object. LIA never calls cbor2; its only path is py_webauthn re-encoding what parse_cbor (cbor2.loads) just decoded from a client's authenticator data. Measured on 6.1.4 (2026-10-03, Windows, whose thread stack is smaller than Linux's): loads refuses container nesting past 400, the deepest structure it accepts (arrays 400, maps and tags 399) re-encodes fine, and a cycle built with value-sharing tags 28/29 is detected by dumps (CBOREncodeValueError, turned into InvalidCBORData by py_webauthn). No release patches it yet: take the fix when it ships.

subject: eslint 9

subject: python 3.10
reason: The self-host installer's floor (ADR-215): it runs on a bare host's own Python, and Ubuntu 22.04 ships 3.10 with standard support until 2027-06-01. The application itself runs 3.14.

subject: squid 6
reason: Upstream line past support; the demonstrator's egress proxy runs Ubuntu 24.04's package instead (ubuntu/squid:6.6-24.04_edge, squid 6.14-0ubuntu0.24.04.2), which Canonical maintains in main until 2029. The image lags two updates (.3 and .4: CVE-2026-47729, FTP gateway; CVE-2026-50012, cache digests), both unreachable through infrastructure/demo-instance/squid.conf: only CONNECT to five provider hosts on 443 passes, with no cache and no peer. Re-read when Canonical rebuilds the image.

subject: pip:aiohttp@3.14.4
reason: The repository advisory contradicts itself: its range reads '>=2,<=3.14.4' while its patched version is 3.14.4. The 3.14.4 release notes carry the fix (multipart handling moved to spooled temporary files to bound the file descriptors), 3.14.5 adds no security change, and the seven sibling advisories published with 3.14.4 read '<=3.14.3'. LIA runs no aiohttp server. Lifted when the advisory's range is corrected, or by the next aiohttp floor.

subject: pip:apscheduler@3.11.2
reason: Needs a persistent job store: the advisory is pickle.loads() on a stored job_state, which only the SQLAlchemy, MongoDB, Redis, RethinkDB and ZooKeeper stores read. LIA builds one AsyncIOScheduler() with no jobstores argument (apps/api/src/main.py), so every job lives in the default in-memory store and nothing is ever unpickled; the account export's one-shot entry is in-memory too (domains/account_export/models.py). No release patches the 3.x line yet: take the fix when it ships, and re-read this acceptance before configuring any persistent store.

subject: npm:@vitest/mocker@4.1.11
reason: Test tooling only: @vitest/mocker ships with vitest, which runs the web suite under jsdom on a developer machine and in CI. The advisory needs vitest's manual-mock registration reachable by an attacker (browser mode or an exposed vitest server); LIA runs neither browser mode nor `vitest --api`/UI, and nothing of vitest reaches a production image. Take 4.1.12 at the next frontend tooling refresh.

subject: pip:caldav@3.3.1
reason: Low: `vcal.fix` normalisation is quadratic on a very large iCalendar object. Its only input is the calendar server of the person's own iCloud connector, read for that person alone; no third party reaches it. 3.3.2 lands at the next Python refresh, after its cooldown, rather than as a release-day lock change.
